title: MYOPATHY, MYOFIBRILLAR, 9, WITH EARLY RESPIRATORY FAILURE
alt_titles: MYOPATHY, PROXIMAL, WITH EARLY RESPIRATORY MUSCLE INVOLVEMENT
HEREDITARY MYOPATHY WITH EARLY RESPIRATORY FAILURE
MYOPATHY, DISTAL, WITH EARLY RESPIRATORY FAILURE, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

relationships.phenotype: MYOPATHY, MYOFIBRILLAR, 9, WITH EARLY RESPIRATORY FAILURE

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding titin (TTN; 188840).

checks.claim: Myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding titin (TTN).
checks.evidence_quote: Our results therefore indicate that TTN mutations are an additional cause of MFM, and that HMERF caused by the p.C30071R mutation in TTN should be classified as MFM-titinopathy.
checks.explanation: The paper reports heterozygous TTN mutations (p.C30071R; 'Sequencing identified the heterozygous g.274375T>C mutation (p.C30071R)') in families with HMERF/MFM and concludes that TTN mutations cause MFM with early respiratory failure. 'MFM9' is OMIM's own name for the disorder and is not in the paper, but it just relabels the condition the paper describes.

paragraphs.text: Myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9), or hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure (HMERF), is an autosomal dominant myopathy (Nicolao et al., 1999) that begins in mid-adult life (Chinnery et al., 2001). Weakness may be predominantly distal or proximal (Pfeffer et al., 2012). The respiratory muscles are involved early in the disease (Nicolao et al., 1999), and respiratory failure develops while affected individuals can still walk (Birchall et al., 2005). Muscle biopsies show myofibrillar changes with cytoplasmic bodies (Pfeffer et al., 2014), eosinophilic inclusions, and rimmed vacuoles (Chinnery et al., 2001).

checks.claim: Myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9), also called hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure (HMERF), is an autosomal dominant myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Two Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy, who also had proximal weakness, early respiratory failure, and characteristic cytoplasmic bodies in the affected muscle biopsies
checks.explanation: The paper describes an autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure. The names MFM9 and HMERF are OMIM's labels for this disorder; the paper does not use them, but that is a naming convention, not a difference in substance.

checks.claim: MFM9 begins in mid-adult life.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a novel autosomal dominant myopathy presenting in mid-adult life with tibialis anterior weakness.
checks.explanation: The abstract says onset is in mid-adult life. The paper describes this family's disorder, and the draft treats it as MFM9.

checks.claim: Weakness in MFM9 may be predominantly distal or predominantly proximal.
checks.evidence_quote: The clinical presentation included predominant distal, proximal or respiratory muscle weakness.
checks.explanation: The abstract says weakness was predominantly distal or proximal.

checks.claim: The respiratory muscles are involved early in MFM9.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal dominant myopathy with proximal weakness and early respiratory muscle involvement maps to chromosome 2q.
checks.explanation: The title says the respiratory muscles are involved early.

checks.claim: In MFM9, respiratory failure develops while affected individuals are still ambulant.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently described a dominant limb myopathy characterised by early respiratory failure whilst affected individuals were still ambulant (autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure).
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the disorder as having early respiratory failure while affected individuals were still ambulant. This is the same as the draft's claim, and the disorder named in the abstract matches HMERF/MFM9.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in MFM9 show myofibrillar changes with cytoplasmic bodies.
checks.evidence_quote: previous work on patients with the p.C30071R mutation has demonstrated Z-disc streaming, cytoplasmic bodies, and evidence of myofibrillar aggregation, further evidence that this condition represents a subtype of MFM.
checks.explanation: Cytoplasmic bodies are reported only from earlier work and in F.7, who carries a novel variant of uncertain significance. The p.C30071R biopsies in this study showed aggregates and inclusions, but cytoplasmic bodies were not described.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in MFM9 show eosinophilic inclusions.
checks.evidence_quote: Fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and vacuoles with basophilic rims were seen in moderately affected muscles
checks.explanation: The abstract reports eosinophilic inclusions in muscle pathology.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in MFM9 show rimmed vacuoles.
checks.evidence_quote: Fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and vacuoles with basophilic rims were seen in moderately affected muscles
checks.explanation: 'Vacuoles with basophilic rims' means rimmed vacuoles.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2014) suggested that HMERF due to mutations in the TTN gene be classified as MFM-titinopathy.

checks.claim: Pfeffer et al. (2014) suggested that HMERF due to TTN mutations be classified as MFM-titinopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We suggest that HMERF due to mutations in the TTN gene be nosologically classified as MFM-titinopathy.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Edstrom et al. (1990) described 16 patients from 7 pedigrees with an unusual limb-girdle myopathy that began in adulthood. A prominent early finding in all cases was respiratory muscle weakness. Muscle biopsy showed myofibrillar changes.

checks.claim: Edstrom et al. (1990) described 16 patients from 7 pedigrees with an unusual limb-girdle myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: 16 patients representing 7 different pedigrees exhibited an unusual, adult onset limb-girdle myopathy with typical clinical hallmarks.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The limb-girdle myopathy in the 16 patients described by Edstrom et al. (1990) began in adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: 16 patients representing 7 different pedigrees exhibited an unusual, adult onset limb-girdle myopathy
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the myopathy as adult onset.

checks.claim: Respiratory muscle weakness was a prominent early finding in all 16 patients described by Edstrom et al. (1990).
checks.evidence_quote: A prominent early finding in all cases was respiratory muscle weakness
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsy in the patients described by Edstrom et al. (1990) showed myofibrillar changes.
checks.evidence_quote: Muscle biopsy findings revealed myofibrillar changes
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Chinnery et al. (2001) reported a family with an autosomal dominant distal myopathy with early respiratory failure that presented in mid-adult life. Moderately affected muscles showed eosinophilic inclusions and rimmed vacuoles. The disease was not linked to any of the known loci associated with distal myopathies.

checks.claim: Chinnery et al. (2001) reported a family with an autosomal dominant distal myopathy with early respiratory failure.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease was not linked to any of the known loci associated with distal myopathies, confirming that the disorder in this family is both genetically and phenotypically distinct.
checks.explanation: The title calls it an 'autosomal dominant distal myopathy with early respiratory failure', and the abstract refers to 'this family', a single three-generation kindred.

checks.claim: The distal myopathy in the family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) presented in mid-adult life.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a novel autosomal dominant myopathy presenting in mid-adult life with tibialis anterior weakness.
checks.explanation: The abstract states onset in mid-adult life.

checks.claim: Moderately affected muscles in the family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) showed eosinophilic inclusions.
checks.evidence_quote: Fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and vacuoles with basophilic rims were seen in moderately affected muscles
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly for moderately affected muscles.

checks.claim: Moderately affected muscles in the family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) showed rimmed vacuoles.
checks.evidence_quote: Fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and vacuoles with basophilic rims were seen in moderately affected muscles
checks.explanation: Vacuoles with basophilic rims are rimmed vacuoles, seen in moderately affected muscles.

checks.claim: The disease in the family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) was not linked to any of the known distal myopathy loci.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease was not linked to any of the known loci associated with distal myopathies
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2012) reported further families with HMERF. The predominant pattern of weakness varied between distal, proximal, and respiratory muscle weakness, and respiratory failure appeared early. Muscle MRI showed characteristic semitendinosus involvement, including in presymptomatic patients. Muscle histopathology most frequently showed eosinophilic inclusions and rimmed vacuoles. Cardiomyopathy was not present in any of the patients.

checks.claim: Pfeffer et al. (2012) reported additional families with HMERF.
checks.evidence_quote: This segregated with the phenotype in 21 individuals from the original family, nine subjects in a second family with the same highly selective pattern of muscle involvement on magnetic resonance imaging and a third familial case with a similar phenotype.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a second family and a third familial case in addition to the original family.

checks.claim: In the HMERF families reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012), the predominant pattern of weakness varied between distal, proximal, and respiratory muscle weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: The clinical presentation included predominant distal, proximal or respiratory muscle weakness.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: In the HMERF families reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012), respiratory failure appeared early.
checks.evidence_quote: This disease should be considered in patients with adult-onset proximal or distal myopathy and early respiratory failure, even in the presence of non-specific muscle pathology.
checks.explanation: The title and abstract describe early respiratory failure in patients who can still walk.

checks.claim: Muscle MRI in the HMERF patients reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012) showed characteristic semitendinosus involvement.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed characteristic abnormalities with semitendinosus involvement in 20 of 21 patients studied, including 3 patients who were presymptomatic
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Semitendinosus involvement on muscle MRI was seen in presymptomatic HMERF patients reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012).
checks.evidence_quote: semitendinosus involvement in 20 of 21 patients studied, including 3 patients who were presymptomatic
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Eosinophilic inclusions were the most frequent histopathologic finding in the HMERF patients reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012).
checks.evidence_quote: Diagnostic muscle histopathology most frequently revealed eosinophilic inclusions (inclusion bodies) and rimmed vacuoles
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Rimmed vacuoles were among the most frequent histopathologic findings in the HMERF patients reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012).
checks.evidence_quote: Diagnostic muscle histopathology most frequently revealed eosinophilic inclusions (inclusion bodies) and rimmed vacuoles
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: None of the HMERF patients reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012) had cardiomyopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Cardiomyopathy was not present in any of our patients despite up to 31 years of follow-up.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: In most of the cases described by Edstrom et al. (1990), there was evidence of autosomal dominant inheritance. The family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) showed autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: Most of the cases described by Edstrom et al. (1990) showed evidence of autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: In a majority of cases there was evidence of an autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) showed autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a novel autosomal dominant myopathy presenting in mid-adult life with tibialis anterior weakness. We carried out a detailed clinical assessment of 24 individuals spanning three generations
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the family's disorder as autosomal dominant.

paragraphs.text: Nicolao et al. (1999) studied 2 Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy, proximal weakness, and early respiratory failure. Using the combined linkage data from both families, they established linkage to chromosome 2q24-q31.

checks.claim: Nicolao et al. (1999) studied 2 Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Two Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The 2 Swedish families studied by Nicolao et al. (1999) had proximal weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: Two Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy, who also had proximal weakness
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The 2 Swedish families studied by Nicolao et al. (1999) had early respiratory failure.
checks.evidence_quote: who also had proximal weakness, early respiratory failure, and characteristic cytoplasmic bodies
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Using combined linkage data from the 2 Swedish families, Nicolao et al. (1999) established linkage of the myopathy to chromosome 2q24-q31.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage to the chromosomal region 2q24-q31 was established. A maximum combined two-point LOD score of 4.87 at a recombination fraction of 0 was obtained with marker D2S1245.
checks.explanation: Linkage to 2q24-q31 was established, and the LOD score combines data from both families.

paragraphs.text: Lange et al. (2005) reported that a human mutation in the titin protein kinase domain caused hereditary muscle disease by disrupting the titin kinase-nbr1-p62-MuRF2 signaling pathway.

checks.claim: Lange et al. (2005) reported that a human mutation in the titin protein kinase domain causes hereditary muscle disease.
checks.evidence_quote: A human mutation in the titin protein kinase domain causes hereditary muscle disease by disrupting this pathway.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Lange et al. (2005) reported that the titin kinase domain mutation disrupts the titin kinase-nbr1-p62-MuRF2 signaling pathway.
checks.evidence_quote: A human mutation in the titin protein kinase domain causes hereditary muscle disease by disrupting this pathway.
checks.explanation: The abstract earlier describes "this pathway" as titin kinase to nbr1 to p62 to MuRF2, so the draft's wording restates it.

paragraphs.text: In the family originally reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) and in additional families, Pfeffer et al. (2012) identified a likely causal variant in the TTN gene, a g.274375T-C change resulting in a cys30071-to-arg (C30071R) substitution. The variant segregated with the phenotype and lay within a haplotype on chromosome 2 that the families shared.

checks.claim: Pfeffer et al. (2012) studied the family originally reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) and additional families with myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure.
checks.evidence_quote: This segregated with the phenotype in 21 individuals from the original family, nine subjects in a second family with the same highly selective pattern of muscle involvement on magnetic resonance imaging and a third familial case with a similar phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract refers to the original family it described in 2001 ('In 2001, we described...') plus additional families. It does not name Chinnery et al. (2001) or use the term 'myofibrillar myopathy-9'; it calls the disorder hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure.

checks.claim: Pfeffer et al. (2012) identified a likely causal variant in the TTN gene in these families: a g.274375T-C change.
checks.evidence_quote: A combination of genome-wide linkage and whole exome sequencing revealed the likely causal genetic variant in the titin (TTN) gene (g.274375T>C; p.Cys30071Arg)
checks.explanation: The abstract states the variant directly.

checks.claim: The TTN g.274375T-C variant results in a cys30071-to-arg (C30071R) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: titin (TTN) gene (g.274375T>C; p.Cys30071Arg)
checks.explanation: The abstract gives the same protein change in equivalent notation.

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R variant segregated with the phenotype in the families studied by Pfeffer et al. (2012).
checks.evidence_quote: This segregated with the phenotype in 21 individuals from the original family, nine subjects in a second family with the same highly selective pattern of muscle involvement on magnetic resonance imaging and a third familial case with a similar phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the variant segregated with the phenotype in these families.

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R variant lay within a haplotype on chromosome 2 that the families studied by Pfeffer et al. (2012) shared.
checks.evidence_quote: within a shared haplotype of 2.93 Mbp on chromosome 2
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions a shared haplotype on chromosome 2 but does not say that all the families shared it. It may have been shared only within the original family, which the linkage analysis would suggest.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2014) found that heterozygous mutations in the TTN gene cause HMERF. The C30071R mutation lies in the 119th fibronectin type III domain, in the A-band of titin.

checks.claim: Pfeffer et al. (2014) found that heterozygous TTN mutations cause HMERF.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing identified the heterozygous g.274375T>C mutation (p.C30071R) in 5/127 unrelated subjects (F.1A, F.2A, F3, F.4B and F.5)
checks.explanation: Heterozygous TTN mutations were found in HMERF/MFM families and co-segregated with disease.

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R mutation lies in the 119th fibronectin type III domain of titin.
checks.evidence_quote: p.C30071R in the 119th fibronectin-3 (FN3) domain
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R mutation lies in the A-band of titin.
checks.evidence_quote: two novel titin (TTN) gene mutations, affecting residues in the A-band of the protein at p.C30071R and p.R32450W
checks.explanation: Stated directly.
